note:
**The 1881 round, schedules 249 to 261 - the end of the book.** Lenton Road, Park Ravine and Standard Hill, transcribed by A. Hagues. **The enumerator's book closes at 261.**

**The last stretch leaves The Park.** Schedules 254 to 261 are on **Standard Hill**, which is the district's name rather than the estate's ground, and the record holds no property there. Those eight households are unfiled with the street written out. They are kept rather than dropped because the district is what the enumerator walked, and because the people in them - a professor of music, a railway manager who was also a Justice of the Peace, a banker's clerk boarding with three Norfolk sisters - belong to the same few streets' worth of lives.

**Two households the record already knew, now confirmed ten years on.** **William Ebenezer Dobson at 23 Lenton Road**, whom the record held in 1871 at 44, is here at 54 - a magistrate and lace dresser employing 105 hands, widowed, with seven children and five servants. And **John W Bowers at Ravine House, 21 Lenton Road**, Alderman and Magistrate, whom the record already holds there in 1891.

**Schedule 249 has no head.** The sheet is cut at the top of the page and 19 Lenton Road opens with three housemaids. Whoever they worked for is on the sheet before, which has not been read.

**Park Ravine is on the page and barely in the record.** John A Wilson, a hosiery manufacturer of 27, is there with an undergraduate of St John's, Cambridge visiting, and one uninhabited house beside them. The record holds only **2 Park Ravine**; the page gives no number, so the household is unfiled.

**Readings that could go either way are flagged in the source line.** Repeated names carry a birth year and are matched on it.
source: 1881 census enumerator's book, Standard Hill and Limits of the Castle of Nottingham, schedules 249 to 261 - the end of the book - transcribed by A. Hagues.
